Showers are in this week’s forecast—but we're not talking rain: When to watch for meteors

Stargazers across the country could see a few bright meteors streaking across the sky this week as the Northern Taurid meteor shower reaches its peak.

LOUISVILLE, Ky. —

The Taurid meteor shower could bring some fireballs to the night sky this week as it reaches its peak.

The Taurids are a lower-quantity, higher-quality show, which means there aren't many, but the few that you do see may be bright!

Catching one of these could be the best "shooting star" you see all year.

The shower is here through December 10, and under ideal viewing conditions, the Northern Taurids peak produces roughly five meteors per hour.

The best chance to see them in our area will be overnight Wednesday or Thursday.

The Taurids are known for occasionally generating exceptionally bright meteors called fireballs, which can make even a relatively quiet night of sky watching memorable.

The sky should be exceptionally dark because the moon will be a waxing crescent and only 5% illuminated.

The problem, however, could be the clouds.

Late Wednesday evening, Impact Weather returns as a low-pressure system swings into the Ohio Valley, producing scattered showers.

This may impact viewing during peak shower hours.

Hearst Owned

Rain moving in Wednesday

If you strike out on catching one of the Northern Taurids this week, you'll have another chance to wish upon a star later this month.

The Leonids Meteor Shower becomes the focus of attention during the early morning hours of November 17 or 18, once the Moon has dropped below the horizon.

With favorable conditions, observers could see as many as 15 meteors per hour.
